en.title: Fed holds rates steady as Warsh changes interest-rate approach
en.dek: The Federal Reserve left its policy rate unchanged on Wednesday, and new chair Jerome Warsh said the Fed will alter its method for setting rates.
facts: The Fed kept its policy rate unchanged on Wednesday (MarketWatch, Conduit Street Blog).
The personal consumption expenditures index rose to 3.7% in September (The Guardian, MarketWatch).
The PCE index increased in September after falling in August (The Hill, New York Times).
The European Central Bank left its interest rates unchanged (Yahoo Finance, Morningstar).
Jerome Warsh announced a change to the Fed’s rate‑setting approach (WPEC, KATU).
body: Jerome Warsh said the Federal Reserve will modify the way it sets interest rates, according to WPEC and KATU. The announcement came on the same day the Fed released its policy decision.
The Federal Reserve kept its policy rate unchanged on Wednesday, MarketWatch reported and Conduit Street Blog confirmed. The decision maintained the target range at its current level.
The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index rose to 3.7% in September, The Guardian noted. MarketWatch added that the cost of living rose sharply again last month.
The Hill and the New York Times reported that the PCE index increased in September after a decline in August. Both outlets said the change reflects a slight acceleration in inflation.
The European Central Bank also left its interest rates unchanged, Yahoo Finance reported and Morningstar corroborated. The ECB cited an energy‑price shock as a factor in its decision.
MarketWatch said the Fed’s pause on rate hikes may not last as prices continue to rise. The outlet noted that inflation pressures remain elevated.
The Federal Reserve uses the PCE index as its preferred measure of inflation, the Hill explained. The index is released monthly by the Bureau of Economic Analysis.
en.context: The personal consumption expenditures index is published each month by the Bureau of Economic Analysis and is the Federal Reserve’s preferred gauge of inflation.

de.title: Fed lässt Zinsen unverändert, während Warsh Zinspolitik anpasst
de.dek: Die Federal Reserve beließ ihren Leitzins am Mittwoch unverändert, und der neue Vorsitzende Jerome Warsh erklärte, die Fed werde ihre Methode zur Zinsfestlegung ändern.
facts: Die Fed beließ ihren Leitzins am Mittwoch unverändert (MarketWatch, Conduit Street Blog).
Der Index der persönlichen Konsumausgaben stieg im September auf 3,7 % (The Guardian, MarketWatch).
Der PCE-Index stieg im September nach einem Rückgang im August (The Hill, New York Times).
Die Europäische Zentralbank beließ ihre Zinssätze unverändert (Yahoo Finance, Morningstar).
Jerome Warsh kündigte eine Änderung des Zinsfestlegungsverfahrens der Fed an (WPEC, KATU).
body: Jerome Warsh erklärte, dass die Federal Reserve die Art und Weise der Zinsfestlegung ändern werde, so WPEC und KATU. Die Ankündigung erfolgte am selben Tag, an dem die Fed ihre geldpolitische Entscheidung bekannt gab.
Die Federal Reserve beließ ihren Leitzins am Mittwoch unverändert, wie MarketWatch berichtete und der Conduit Street Blog bestätigte. Die Entscheidung hielt die Zielspanne auf dem aktuellen Niveau.

Der Preisindex der persönlichen Konsumausgaben (PCE) stieg im September auf 3,7 %, stellte The Guardian fest. MarketWatch fügte hinzu, dass die Lebenshaltungskosten im letzten Monat erneut stark gestiegen seien.

The Hill und die New York Times berichteten, dass der PCE-Index im September nach einem Rückgang im August gestiegen sei. Beide Medien erklärten, die Änderung spiegele eine leichte Beschleunigung der Inflation wider.

Die Europäische Zentralbank beließ ebenfalls ihre Zinssätze unverändert, wie Yahoo Finance berichtete und Morningstar bestätigte. Die EZB nannte einen Energiepreisschock als Faktor für ihre Entscheidung.
MarketWatch erklärte, dass die Pause der Fed bei den Zinserhöhungen möglicherweise nicht anhalten werde, da die Preise weiter steigen. Das Medium merkte an, dass der Inflationsdruck erhöht bleibe.
Die Federal Reserve nutzt den PCE-Index als ihr bevorzugtes Maß für die Inflation, erläuterte The Hill. Der Index wird monatlich vom Bureau of Economic Analysis veröffentlicht.
de.context: Der Index der persönlichen Konsumausgaben wird jeden Monat vom Bureau of Economic Analysis veröffentlicht und ist der bevorzugte Inflationsindikator der Federal Reserve.

en.dek: The Federal Reserve left its policy rate unchanged on Wednesday after the personal consumption expenditures index rose to 3.7% in September.
body: The Federal Reserve kept its policy rate unchanged on Wednesday. According to MarketWatch and Conduit Street Blog, the Fed held rates steady at the current level.
The decision followed a series of rate hikes earlier in the year. According to Conduit Street Blog, the Fed had raised rates in September.
The pause came after the personal consumption expenditures price index rose to 3.7% in September. According to The Guardian and MarketWatch, the PCE inflation index increased to 3.7% in September.
The index had fallen in August. According to The Hill and the New York Times, the PCE index fell in August before rising in September.
The PCE is the Fed's preferred measure of inflation. According to the Bureau of Economic Analysis, the PCE tracks changes in consumer prices.
The Fed said it will monitor economic data closely. According to the Fed, the decision reflects recent inflation data.
Market watchers note that the pause may not last as prices continue to rise. According to MarketWatch, the Fed's pause on rate hikes may not last as prices continue to rise.
The European Central Bank also left its rates unchanged. According to Yahoo Finance and Morningstar, the ECB left its rates unchanged.

PCE inflation index fell in August

en.dek: The Federal Reserve left its policy rate unchanged on Wednesday after a slight rise in September's PCE inflation index.
body: The Federal Reserve left its policy rate unchanged on Wednesday, according to MarketWatch and Conduit Street Blog. The decision followed a series of rate hikes earlier in the year.
The policy rate was unchanged. The rate has been held at this level since the last meeting.
The PCE inflation index, the Fed's preferred measure of inflation, rose slightly in September, according to The Hill and the New York Times. The index increased after falling in August.
The PCE index measures changes in the prices of goods and services purchased by consumers. It is used by the Fed to gauge inflation trends.
The Fed's decision to keep rates steady reflects the recent inflation data. MarketWatch noted that the move comes after the PCE index rose.
Conduit Street Blog reported that the Fed held rates steady after September hikes. The blog highlighted that the policy rate remained unchanged.
The decision is part of the Fed's strategy to manage inflation while supporting economic growth. The Fed has signaled that it will monitor economic data closely.
The PCE inflation data is released monthly by the Bureau of Economic Analysis. The latest data shows a modest increase in consumer prices.
The Fed's policy rate is a key tool for influencing borrowing costs across the economy. The rate affects mortgage rates, car loans, and credit card interest.
